newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy deputy P.M. says coalition solid.
newsitem.headline: Italy deputy P.M. says coalition solid.

text.p: Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said on Thursday that a meeting of leaders of parties which support Italy's centre-left government had resolved strains over employment.

"The situation has been unblocked," Veltroni told reporters. "There is political solidarity in the (parliamentary) majority and this coalition confirms that it intends to last for the entire legislature," he said.
Details were not immediately available on any agreement reached by the parties in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition.

The meeting was called to discuss government proposals to boost employment. The plans have created strains in an already tense coalition, with hard-left ally Communist Refoundation threatening to vote down the measures.
Refoundation lies outside the coalition but guarantees its majority in the lower house of parliament. Party leader Fausto Bertinotti attended Thursday's coalition summit.
Veltroni said trades union leaders would meet the government later on Thursday to discuss the employment issue. The cabinet will also meet on jobs on Friday morning.
